## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V

# Child 2: Bot-created children must not silently demote completed/in_review parents

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 2a).

## Problem statement

`demoteParentOnChildAdded` (`database.ts:1566-1585`, via `create.ts:252-286`, `update.ts:489`) rewinds any `completed`/`in_review` parent to `open`/`plan_complete` on child attach. The triage/test bot auto-attaches `[test-failure]` children (e.g. WL-0MTUOJLA9008JSTZ attached to WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 on 2026-09-09), which keeps an otherwise-finished parent (F1-F3 all `completed/done`) permanently non-terminal. The parent then reads as "revived work" even though its planned scope is done and its audit verdict already recorded.

Human-added missed subtasks (the original WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 intent) must still demote.

## Users

- **Producer:** a finished parent with all planned children done should stay finished; bot telemetry should not reopen it.
- **Triage bot:** must still record test failures visibly (as children or linked items) without rewinding parent lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Attaching a child authored by automation (`triage-bot`, `test` skill `check_or_create`, or `[test-failure]`-titled items) to a `completed`/`in_review` parent does NOT move the parent to `open`/`plan_complete`. Decide and document one behavior: skip demotion, or attach as non-blocking link/reference instead of child.
- [ ] Human-attached missed subtasks still demote the parent (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 behavior preserved) with a regression test.
- [ ] Regression test: bot-child attach leaves parent status/stage untouched; human-child attach demotes.
- [ ] Existing create/update/demotion tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Preserve WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 intent for human-added children.
- Bot failure telemetry must remain discoverable (no silent dropping).

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:1566-1585` — `demoteParentOnChildAdded`
- `src/commands/create.ts:252-286`, `src/commands/update.ts:489`
- Triage/test-failure creation path (`test` skill `check_or_create.py` or equivalent)

- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC2:** Attaching a bot-created child does not silently rewind the parent — primary fix.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC4:** Regression test: bot-child attach leaves parent untouched; human-child demotes.

# Child 3: Demotion must leave an audit-trail comment + queue surfaces must ignore mechanical churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 2b + surfacing).

## Problem statement

Two observability gaps make revivals confusing:

1. **Silent demotion.** When `demoteParentOnChildAdded` fires, nothing is recorded on the parent. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's comment history ends at its passing audit (2026-09-03); the 2026-09-06 demotion (child WL-0MTQ2FGSK004CBRK attached) left no trace, so the item's return to `open/plan_complete` looks inexplicable.
2. **Churn-sensitive surfaces.** `wl recent`, recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`), and heartbeat selection treat re-sort-stamped `updatedAt` as genuine activity, so bulk-touched items (13-item and 88-item clusters on 2026-09-11, incl. WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC which never actually progressed) surface as "freshly active."

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** needs to see *why* an item went back to open, and needs `recent`/`next` to reflect real work, not mechanical churn.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `demoteParentOnChildAdded` demotion writes a comment on the parent: which child was attached, by whom/what, from→to status/stage, timestamp.
- [ ] `wl recent` and recency scoring distinguish semantic edits from sortIndex-only touches (builds on Child 1; if Child 1 stops the stamping, this AC reduces to verifying `recent` ordering is clean — document which approach was taken).
- [ ] Regression test: attach child to completed parent → parent carries the demotion comment with child id + actor.
- [ ] Existing tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Comment format should match existing `wl comment` conventions (author attribution for bot vs human actor).
- Coordinate with Child 1: if `updatedAt` is no longer stamped by re-sort, verify rather than re-implement churn filtering here.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:1566-1585` — demotion point (add comment write)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:2215-2216` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/recent.ts` (or equivalent) — recent listing
- `skill/heartbeat/scripts/heartbeat.py` — heartbeat selection

## Parent AC coverage

- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC3:** Queue surfaces distinguish semantic edits from mechanical timestamp churn — audit-trail comments + coordinated fix with Child 1.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC4:** Regression test: demotion writes comment with child id + actor.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC5:** Full suite passes (all children contribute).

## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to open at most one pane per work item per skill while a prior dispatch is still in-flight, so concurrent agents never share a worktree/branch or fight over the same files.

## Problem Statement

On 2026-09-21 the downtime dispatcher spawned `/skill:implement` twice for two different critical items (LP-0MUAY98ZR002JBAA, LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO) within minutes-to-hours of each other. Both dispatched agents operated on the same worktree and branch concurrently, causing file conflicts, thrashed edits, discarded work, and wasted compute (~2h20m45s on LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO). This is a recurrence of WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT (prior RCA covering audit/plan tiers) in the implement tier, affecting critical-priority items.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** Runs the herdr downtime dispatcher and expects it to correctly serialize dispatches.
- **Pi agent (AI):** Receives auto-dispatches from herdr and works on assigned items.
- **System administrator:** Monitors herdr performance and resource usage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Root cause confirmed:** The selection path and mechanism that produced the 13:54:33Z re-dispatch of LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO are confirmed (H1: critical-first scan bypasses marker exclusion / H2: stale item status in dispatcher snapshot / H3: non-atomic rolling-log rewrite / H4: multiple leaders) via targeted instrumentation or reproduction.

- **AC2 — Duplicate-dispatch prevention:** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.

- **AC3 — Escalation preserved:** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

- **AC4 — Atomic rolling log:** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

- **AC5 — Regression test:** An integration test covering both the Herdr-head and coordination dispatch paths verifies that two idle cycles with a critical implement item already claimed/in-flight at the same stage produce exactly one dispatch.

- **AC6 — Dispatcher log enriched:** Each dispatcher log entry records the session/pane id and the selection path/reason, extending the current schema (`itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`) to support automated RCA.

## Constraints

- Changes must be in TypeScript (`packages/herdr/src/`) and use the existing dispatch marker lifecycle.
- The rolling log must remain human-readable JSONL.
- Escalation for stuck critical items must not be eliminated — only the duplicate-dispatch bug must be fixed.
- The fix should work within the existing single-leader model; multi-leader support is out of scope.

## Existing State

- Dispatcher selection uses two paths: (1) normal Herdr-head scan via `classifyItemForDispatch` (filters `status === 'open'`, consults dispatched-marker exclusion), and (2) critical-first scan via `dispatchClaimedTier` (CAS claim only, bypasses marker exclusion).
- Dispatched markers (`downtime-log.ts:273,310`) exclude items only while `marker.stage === itemStage` AND age ≤ staleness window (default 24h, hard floor 1h, ceiling 7d).
- The critical-first scan intentionally bypasses marker exclusion at `downtime-worker.ts:1935-1966`.
- Rolling logs are rewritten non-atomically (read-all → append → trim → write), creating a TOCTOU window.
- The first dispatch of each duplicate pair claimed the item (`status: in_progress`) but the stage stayed `plan_complete` (a prior `WARNING: Failed to update stage`).
- WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN added conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed). This is the implement-tier recurrence.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatcher selection and dispatch logic (critical-first scan at ~line 1895, normal scan at ~line 2455, dispatch site at ~line 2710-2745)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Dispatched markers and rolling log management (markers at ~line 273, 310; appendRollingJsonl at ~line 411-431)
- `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` — Canonical tool for scanning duplicate dispatches

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed) — prior audit/plan-tier RCA.
- **WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN** — Downtime dispatcher: conditional claim + plan/intake marker exclusion (completed) — implement-tier fix for a different path.
- **WL-0MT32F908002YFFA** — Downtime dispatch: recover items stranded by marker-write-failed or spawn failure (open) — interacts with marker lifecycle.
- **WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY** — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions (completed).
- Code-referenced: WL-0MU6UL0RJ008IHGT (marker staleness), WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT (critical-first scan), WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 (Herdr-list-head dispatch).

## Out of Scope

- Other pre-existing duplicate pairs from before 2026-09-21.
- The correctness of code delivered by LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO (already merged to `dev`).
- Multi-leader/leader-failover support for the dispatcher.

## Risks & Assumptions

**Risks:**
- Changing the critical-first scan to consult markers may slow escalation of genuinely blocked critical items. *Mitigation:* bound escalation with a TTL or in-flight check (AC3).
- Atomic log rewrite changes file semantics; existing consumers must handle it. *Mitigation:* JSONL format preserved, `rename` is transparent.
- Regression test requires simulating dispatch cycles; test complexity may be high. *Mitigation:* leverage existing Herdr test infrastructure.

**Assumptions:**
- `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` is the authoritative dispatch record.
- The 13:54:33Z dispatch was not a legitimate operator-initiated retry.
- Single-leader model holds; no concurrent workers on this instance.
- The `status: in_progress` claim by the first agent was the only serialisation mechanism — the stage never advanced, so marker exclusion never released the item.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

1. **Q:** Is this item scoped to both root-cause analysis AND implementation, or should it be split into an investigation item + a fix item?
   - **A (agent):** Single item is appropriate. The description already contains sufficient investigation to proceed to fix; the investigation is tightly coupled to the fix (AC1 confirms the mechanism before AC2-AC5 implement it). Splitting adds overhead without benefit.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment during intake review.

2. **Q:** For AC3, should escalation of items blocked by stale markers be bound to a fixed interval (e.g., once per 24h) or to a more dynamic mechanism (e.g., check for live pane before re-dispatching)?
   - **A (agent):** Dynamic mechanism is preferred — checking for a live pane / in-flight claim is more robust than a fixed interval. A fixed interval risks either too-frequent checks (wasted cycles) or too-rare checks (stalled items).
   - **Source:** Agent recommendation based on code analysis of the marker lifecycle.

3. **Q:** Should the regression test be a unit test or an integration test?
   - **A (agent):** Integration test — the bug involves the interaction between the dispatcher loop, marker management, and claim lifecycle, which spans multiple functions in the runtime loop.
   - **Source:** Agent assessment of the failure mode.

## Summary

Make audit freshness **content-based** rather than write-time-based, by porting the
canonical content-fingerprint gate from the audit skill (SorraAgents,
SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) into ContextHub.

Today `isAuditFresh()` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`) implements **only** the legacy
60 s time floor against `updatedAt`, so any metadata-only write (comment, sync merge,
lifecycle transition) marks a valid audit stale. A read-only review of the
`completed`/`in_review` queue found **22 of 52 items stale** and **12 with no audit at
all** (~65 % not fresh), almost none because the code actually changed.

## Problem

`updatedAt` is a *write* clock, not a *content* clock. It moves for reasons unrelated
to the audit's validity:

- `createComment` / `updateComment` / `deleteComment` unconditionally call
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`).
- sync merges re-timestamp items (95 items retimestamped to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` in a
  single sync; 244 items conflicted).
- `assignSortIndexValues()` (used by `wl migrate`) still bumps `updatedAt`.
- the audit runner's own verdict-driven status/stage transition happens *after* audit
  persistence and so stales the audit it just wrote.

The canonical algorithm is content-first, with the time gate only as a **legacy
fallback**:

> 1. fingerprint = HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state
>    (`git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD`); unchanged → fresh
> 2. time gate (floor): legacy reports use the 60 s gate

## Expected behaviour

- Each audit record carries a content fingerprint captured at persist time.
- `isAuditFresh` returns fresh when the stored fingerprint equals the current
  fingerprint, **regardless** of `updatedAt` movement caused by comments, sync merges
  or re-sorts.
- Audits without a fingerprint (legacy) fall back to the existing 60 s time gate.
- A genuine change to the auditable content (description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD,
  working-tree state) still invalidates the audit (stale).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `audit_results` gains a nullable `fingerprint` column via migration; existing rows
   are unaffected and remain readable.
2. `wl audit-set` (and the audit runner's `persist_audit.py` / `wl update --audit-text`
   path) records the fingerprint atomically with `audited_at`.
3. A single shared `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)`
   helper is the sole freshness definition; it returns fresh when the fingerprints match.
4. `updatedAt` churn alone (post-audit comment, sync merge re-timestamp, `sortIndex`
   re-sort) does **not** mark a fingerprinted audit stale.
5. A change to the description/ACs, Key Files, HEAD sha, or working-tree state marks
   the audit stale.
6. Legacy audits with no stored fingerprint fall back to the existing time gate
   (unchanged behaviour).
7. `stageDisplayIcon`, `selectAuditCandidate` / `getNextAuditCandidate`, and the
   ordering predicate all consume the same shared helper — no competing comparison.
8. Tests cover: comment-after-audit stays fresh; sync-bump stays fresh; description
   edit goes stale; HEAD change goes stale; legacy fallback.
9. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- canonical algorithm: audit skill `SKILL.md` §Freshness Gate; SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT
- related-to: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (P2 — sync-merge churn)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17),
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` `isAuditFresh`, `packages/shared/src/database.ts`
  `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt`

## Summary

Stop `updatedAt` acting as a catch-all write clock for **comments**, so that a
post-audit comment (session log, dispatch note, audit note, close reason) can no
longer invalidate a valid audit.

## Problem

`createComment`, `updateComment` and `deleteComment` in
`packages/shared/src/database.ts` all call `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()`
unconditionally. The icon freshness predicate (`isAuditFresh`,
`AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS = 60000`) only tolerates comment bumps that
land inside 60 s of the audit. In practice comments arrive minutes or days later:

- `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`: audit `22:04:23`, `updatedAt 22:05:44` — 81 s, just past the
  window.
- `WL-0MTOBZZNU0009MW1` (+ 4 siblings): the `implement` "Start phase aborted" comment
  is the last write before the cluster that staled the audit.

The audit skill already documents this hazard and prescribes ordering (comment
**before** `wl audit-set`), but ordering is fragile and cannot protect against any
comment added later by another session or bot.

## Expected behaviour

- Comment activity is still recorded and visible (ordering, recency, FTS), but it does
  not move the audit-relevant timestamp.
- Semantic content edits (title, description, ACs, tags, parent, status, stage,
  priority, issue type, risk, effort) continue to bump the content timestamp.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A separate activity timestamp (e.g. `activityAt`) is introduced and bumped by
   comment create/update/delete; `updatedAt` is left untouched by comment writes.
2. Audit freshness is computed against the content timestamp, not the activity
   timestamp.
3. Ordering/recency features that currently rely on comment-updated `updatedAt`
   continue to work (or are explicitly re-pointed at `activityAt` with tests).
4. `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT`-class case (audit then transition/comment > 60 s later) stays
   fresh.
5. Tests: add comment after audit → still fresh; delete comment → still fresh;
   description edit after audit → stale.
6. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- related-to: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 (audit freshness after post-audit comments),
  WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R (flag-only flips must not invalidate audits)
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §Safety/prompt design — ordering contract SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM

## Summary

Ensure a just-persisted audit is not invalidated by the audit runner's **own**
verdict-driven lifecycle transition.

## Problem

`persist_audit.py` / `wl audit-set` writes the audit and (atomically) sets
`updatedAt = auditedAt`. The runner then applies the terminal status/stage
transition separately (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`). Because `status` and `stage`
are tracked content fields, that second `wl update` bumps `updatedAt` **after** the
audit, so the item is stale the moment the audit completes.

Observed: `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT` audit `2026-09-20T22:04:23.765Z`, `updatedAt`
`2026-09-20T22:05:44.810Z` — 81 s, just outside the 60 s tolerance. The audit skill
explicitly notes the tolerance "covers the runner's own writes only"; 81 s is
ordinary, so the window is simply too small to be relied on.

## Expected behaviour

- After a successful audit run, the item is fresh immediately and remains fresh until
  real content changes — the runner's own transition never stales its own audit.
- The lifecycle transition still happens and is still recorded.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit is the **last** write for a just-audited item: `auditedAt >= updatedAt`
   after the runner completes (persist `auditedAt` after the lifecycle transition, or
   tag the runner's own transition so freshness ignores it).
2. `isAuditFresh` returns true for the `WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT` shape (audit then
   transition ~80 s later) without widening the global tolerance constant.
3. A genuine post-audit content edit (description/ACs) still stales the audit.
4. Regression test covering the runner's persist→transition ordering.
5. Full test suite passes.

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- audit skill `SKILL.md` §Safety/prompt design — ordering contract SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM
- `persist_audit.py`, `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`

## Summary

Remove the second, competing audit-freshness definition and route every consumer
through the single shared helper.

## Problem

There are two freshness definitions with different semantics:

1. `packages/shared/src/icons.ts`:
   `auditTime > updateTime - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` (60 000 ms,
   one-sided).
2. `packages/shared/src/database.ts` `isAuditNotReadyFresh()`:
   `new Date(audit.auditedAt).getTime() >= new Date(itemUpdatedAt).getTime()`
   (strict `>=`, no tolerance) — used by the ordering boost
   (`sortItemsByScore`, `computeScore`, `selectBySortIndex`).

So the icon and downtime dispatcher can call an item fresh while the ordering tier
treats it as stale (or vice versa) — the exact divergence WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE set out
to remove, which only unified the icon and dispatch paths.

## Expected behaviour

- Exactly one freshness definition exists in the codebase.
- The ordering path, the icon path and the dispatch path agree for every input.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `isAuditNotReadyFresh` is removed or delegates to the shared `isAuditFresh`.
2. No other file re-implements an `auditedAt` vs `updatedAt` comparison.
3. Symmetric at-or-near semantics are used where intended (`|auditedAt - updatedAt| <
   tolerance`), matching the canonical SorraAgents fix, rather than the current
   one-sided comparison.
4. Tests assert icon, dispatch and ordering agree on: fresh, stale, just-persisted,
   and missing-audit inputs.
5. Full test suite passes.

treated as "no audit" by the icon and the downtime dispatcher.

# Context

Planning established that the hypothesis set in the parent description is not sufficient on its own:
the Herdr-head critical-first scan (`selectCriticalFirstCandidates`) only accepts

critical `plan_complete` (implement-kind) item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the critical-first escalation to skip an item that already has a live
dispatch pane, so a critical item whose `status` reverted to `open` is never dispatched twice, while
escalation of genuinely stuck critical items is preserved.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC2** and **AC3**.

# Design (approved at the plan approval gate)

The critical-first scan currently bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion **unconditionally**
(WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT). This replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an
item-scoped live-pane check**, with a marker-TTL fallback when the pane query is unavailable:

```
for a critical-first candidate:
  1. resolve the item-scoped in-flight signal (live dispatch pane whose label suffix is the item id
     and whose agent status is non-terminal)
  2. if a live WORKING pane exists                 -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-pane)
  3. else if the pane query SUCCEEDED and found none -> ESCALATE (reason: no-live-pane)
  4. else (pane query FAILED/unparseable)          -> fall back to the marker TTL:
       fresh marker (age <= markerStaleWindowMs)   -> SKIP  (reason: in-flight-unverified)
       stale/absent marker                         -> ESCALATE (reason: marker-stale-escalation)
```

This deliberate **neither-blind-fail-closed-nor-blind-fail-open** choice was confirmed at the approval
gate: escalation is never starved permanently (the TTL fallback keeps progressing), and a duplicate is
never permitted while a pane is live. Note the fallback is benign in practice — pane spawn itself needs
herdr, so a persistent pane-query failure also prevents dispatch.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC2.1 — Live pane blocks.** With a live `working` downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id,
**no** dispatch is attempted for that item — regardless of marker freshness, stage advancement, or
`status` being `open`.

**AC2.2 — Fail-closed on unknown in-flight state.** A failed or unparseable pane query never results in
a dispatch that could duplicate in-flight work; it resolves via the marker-TTL fallback (AC3.3) and
records the `in-flight-unverified` reason.

**AC2.3 — Terminal panes do not block.** Panes whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` do not block
dispatch (no idle-pane deadlock).

**AC2.4 — Item-scoped only.** The guard never uses a global running-pane count as a dispatch limit —
the WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant is preserved (that count stays a liveness/owner-lease signal only).

**AC2.5 — Normal loop covered.** The guard also applies to critical candidates reaching dispatch
through the normal (non-critical-first) loop, so AC2 holds "regardless of selection path".

**AC3.1 — Escalation preserved.** A critical item with a fresh **or** stale marker and **no** live pane
is still escalated within one idle cycle; all existing critical-first tests stay green.

**AC3.2 — Escalation is bounded.** Deferral happens only while a live working pane exists or while the
marker is fresh during a pane-query outage — never by an unbounded fixed TTL alone.

**AC3.3 — TTL fallback documented.** The fallback bound (`markerStaleWindowMs`, default 24h, floor 1h)
and its rationale are documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

# Minimal implementation

- Add an item-scoped in-flight resolver, resolved **once per idle cycle** and threaded into
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`: extend `RunningPanesResult` to expose pane records (or add a sibling dep
  returning `{paneId, itemId, kind, agentStatus}[]`), reusing `parseHerdrPaneListOutput`.
- Derive the item id from the pane label suffix (`buildDowntimePaneTitle` preserves `- <itemId>` as a
  suffix via `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`).
- Replace the critical-first loop's unconditional marker bypass with the decision table above.
- Factor the resolver so WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI can reuse it unchanged (no logic duplication across paths).
- Fail-open on resolver errors in the sense that the resolver returns "unavailable" (never throws into
  the dispatch loop); fail-closed semantics are the decision table's step 4.
- **Parent AC2 (restated):** A critical-priority item is never dispatched twice for the same skill while a prior dispatch is in-flight (live pane and/or unexpired claim), regardless of marker freshness or stage advancement.
- **Parent AC3 (restated):** The critical-first escalation path retains its ability to progress items blocked by a stale marker, without re-dispatching in-flight items. Escalation is bounded (e.g., once per claim TTL, or gated on a live-pane / in-flight check).

# Dependencies

# Deliverables

  split-by-skill").

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want the dispatch and coordination rolling logs written atomically, so a
concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log and momentarily lose a
duplicate-dispatch marker.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC4**.

# Context

`appendRollingJsonl` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`) rewrites the log non-atomically: read all
lines → push → trim → `writeFile` directly to the target path. A reader arriving during the
`writeFile` can see a truncated or empty file, which makes `dispatchedItemMarkers` /
`dispatchedItemStages` momentarily lose the marker. This is a contributing factor (H3 in the parent
RCA), not the sole cause — it cannot by itself duplicate a critical-tier item, because the
critical-first scan bypasses markers entirely (that is WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO's fix). It is fixed independently
because it is a genuine TOCTOU defect and because it silently weakens every marker-guarded tier.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC4.1 — Atomic replacement.** `appendRollingJsonl` writes to a temporary sibling file and `rename`s it
over the target. A test asserts the target path is never opened for direct writing.

**AC4.2 — No leaked temp files.** No temporary file remains after a successful append, and none remains
after an I/O failure (cleanup happens before the error is rethrown).

**AC4.3 — Concurrent reader never sees a partial log.** A test that hammers append + read in parallel
observes **only** complete, parseable JSONL lines — never an empty file, never a partial line. The test
fails against the pre-fix writer.

**AC4.4 — Contract unchanged.** Trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) and the throw-on-I/O-failure
(fail-closed) contract are unchanged; the file stays human-readable JSONL.

**AC4.5 — Both logs.** Both `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` and the coordination log use the atomic
writer.

**AC4.6 — Same-filesystem rename.** The temp file is created in the same directory as the target so
`rename` is atomic (a cross-device rename would fall back to copy + unlink and lose atomicity).

# Minimal implementation

- Temp file name including pid + random suffix, in the same directory as the target.
- `mkdir(dir, {recursive:true})` unchanged; `readFile`/trim/append logic unchanged; `writeFile` to the
  temp path, then `rename` over the target.
- `try`/`finally`-style cleanup: on any error, best-effort unlink the temp file, then rethrow so the
  caller's fail-closed behaviour (abort the dispatch) is preserved.
- Keep the existing exported signatures so no caller changes are needed.
- **Parent AC4 (restated):** The dispatch and coordination rolling logs use atomic write (write temp file + `rename`) so a concurrent marker read can never observe an empty or partial log.

# Dependencies

None — independently shippable and may land in parallel with WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI.

- Code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Rolling log trimming" update.

# Goal

As a herdr operator, I want every dispatcher log entry to record the session/pane id and the selection
path/reason, so the next duplicate-dispatch RCA is answerable from the log alone instead of by
inference.

Part of parent **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4**. Covers parent **AC6**.

# Context

The current schema is `itemId/kind/dispatchedAt/cwd/title/stage`. Two constraints shape the design:

1. `recordDispatch` runs **before** `spawnAgentPane` (fail-closed ordering: a marker write failure
   aborts the dispatch), and `DowntimeSpawnResult` is `{ok: true}` with no pane id — `send-to-pi.sh` is
   fire-and-forget. The pane/session id is therefore **not** known at marker-write time.
2. `dispatchedItemMarkers` takes the **last** entry per `itemId`, and `markerStillExcludes` is
   fail-closed on a missing/unparseable `dispatchedAt`. Any post-spawn entry must therefore **preserve**
   `dispatchedAt` + `stage` or it would corrupt marker semantics.

Decision at the plan approval gate (Q5): use a **best-effort post-spawn enrichment entry** rather than
extending the spawn contract / `send-to-pi.sh`.

# Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

**AC6.1 — Selection path and reason recorded.** Every successful dispatch entry records
`selectionPath` (e.g. `critical-first` | `normal-scan` | `coordination-offer` | `scheduled-prompt`) and
a machine-readable `selectionReason` (e.g. `marker-stale`, `in-flight-pane`, `no-live-pane`,
`in-flight-unverified`, `non-critical`).

**AC6.2 — Pane/session id recorded without breaking markers.** Successful dispatches record the
resolved pane id via a post-spawn enrichment entry that **preserves** `itemId`, `kind`, `stage` and
`dispatchedAt`; a test round-trips the enriched log through `dispatchedItemMarkers` and
`markerStillExcludes` and proves identical exclusion/release behaviour with and without enrichment.

**AC6.3 — Enrichment is fail-open.** If the pane id cannot be resolved, the dispatch still succeeds and
the log records an explicit absence (no guessed value).

**AC6.4 — Backward compatible.** Legacy entries without the new fields parse and behave exactly as
before; the existing `downtime-log.test.ts` compatibility tests stay green.

**AC6.5 — Tooling reports the new fields.** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` surfaces
`selectionPath`/`selectionReason`/`paneId` for post-fix evidence (and tolerates their absence).

**AC6.6 — Spawn-failed entries unchanged.** `outcome: 'spawn-failed'` entries stay non-excluding
(WL-0MT32F908002YFFA AC2 invariant) with or without the new fields.

# Minimal implementation

- Add `selectionPath`, `selectionReason` and an optional `paneId` to `DowntimeDispatchEvent`.
- Thread the selection path/reason from the selection loops (WL-WL-0MUBVKPLP006RRDJ's per-cycle trace provides the
  vocabulary; WL-WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO/WL-WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI provide the in-flight reasons).
- After a successful spawn, resolve the pane id (label-suffix lookup against `herdr pane list`) and

Design decision (AC1 + AC2):

**AC1 (audit-trail comment):** implemented in the CLI layer (`src/demotion-audit.ts`, `recordDemotionAuditTrail`) and invoked from both attach paths (`create.ts`, `update.ts`) right after a successful demotion. It writes a comment on the parent naming the attached child (id + title), the actor (`child.createdBy` or `system`), the from→to status/stage, and an ISO timestamp, with the child referenced.

Why the CLI layer rather than `packages/shared/src/database.ts`: worktrees symlink `node_modules`, so `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's built `dist` for both runtime and `tsc` type-checking. Changing the shared `demoteParentOnChildAdded` signature breaks the worktree build (TS2554), and shared-only changes are invisible to the worktree test suite. Placing the comment at the CLI layer keeps it fully verifiable. The CLI commands are the sole callers of `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, so every demotion is covered. The write is best-effort: it never undoes the demotion or aborts the attach.

**AC2 (queue surfaces vs churn):** Child 1 (WL-0MU2QKB98007BKYT) removed the `updatedAt` stamping from `batchUpdateSortIndices`, so re-sort no longer counts as activity. AC2 therefore reduces to verifying the `wl recent` surface, covered by `tests/cli/recent-churn-vs-semantic.test.ts` (re-sort leaves ordering and `updatedAt` untouched; a genuine title edit moves the item to the top).
